evals.name: cache-eviction-concept-build
evals.prompt: dan is taking over cache eviction tuning from priya and his plan is to get the whole cache-sim docker setup running on his laptop and speed it up to 10x. thats way overkill imo, we just need to compare eviction policies on the access logs. can you turn these branch notes into a page that explains how to evaluate eviction policies offline and how to build that? notes are in evals/files/edge-cache-branch-notes.md
evals.expected_output: Concept + build (or course-correction) page: an in-process trace replay through each policy, byte vs request hit rate, warm-up/cold start, scan resistance, build steps with validation against production metrics, focus/leave-out that drops docker/nginx/k6/redis, optional extras tier (dashboard, warmup, sizing). No branch name, PR number or people's names.
assertions: page.html exists and passes check_page.py with no errors
No source provenance: no people, PR/ticket numbers or branch names from the source
Supports light and dark themes via tokens
Contains interactive controls (sliders or buttons) wired to toys
Has numbered build steps
Includes a validation step against production / real metrics
Leave-out guidance drops the docker / nginx / k6 setup
Distinguishes byte hit rate from request hit rate
Marks an optional / good-to-have tier
At least 4 toys
